thread.title: Pepperdine's Mountain at Mullin Park enters final phases of construction
thread.title_full: Pepperdine's Mountain at Mullin Park enters final phases of construction

author: m. s. mccall
title: Pepperdine's Mountain at Mullin Park enters final phases of construction
text:
Pepperdine University announced on May 12 that its Mountain at Mullin Park project is entering the final phases of construction this summer. The development will add a 3,600-seat sports arena and a new student center to the Malibu campus.
The project is significant for Pepperdine as it aims to enhance both athletic facilities and student life amenities. University officials say these new spaces are designed to support community engagement and holistic student development.
“Each week, we get closer to welcoming our students to these new state-of-the-art facilities,” said Ben Veenendaal, vice president for Pepperdine’s department of Planning, Operations, and Construction. “The Mountain at Mullin Park is intentionally designed to support the vibrant community of belonging that is integral to Pepperdine, which has been successfully upheld throughout the institution’s history. This summer, we’re positioned to bring the next phase of this remarkable project toward opening for all to enjoy.”
The student center will house the university’s RISE Institute and is expected soon to receive a temporary certificate of occupancy. In the coming months, non-construction personnel may begin preparing the building with furniture and equipment needed for full functionality. The three-floor facility will offer wellness spaces, a fitness center expanding available space from 2,000 square feet in Firestone Fieldhouse to 10,000 square feet in the new building, exercise class areas, and rooms for community activities.
“I’m confident the RISE building, with all of its amenities, will immediately serve as a space of development and growth for our students and broader University community,” Veenendaal said.
Construction on the hardwood basketball and volleyball court inside the arena is scheduled for this summer along with installation of stadium seating through May and June. The arena already includes lighting systems, speakers, air conditioning units, kitchen equipment for concessions and café options.
As interior work nears completion on both buildings, crews are shifting focus outdoors by pouring concrete in plaza areas between them ahead of fall semester activities. This exterior space will provide additional gathering spots nestled between campus landmarks such as the Santa Monica Mountains and Pacific Ocean.
Earlier milestones include completion in January 2025 of an adjacent parking structure offering 825 spaces—including provisions for electric vehicles—supporting daily operations as well as large-scale events like graduations or athletic competitions.
